deities: Lord Mallikarjuna (Shiva in Jyotirlinga form, self-manifested; 'lord of jasmine flowers')
Goddess Bhramaramba/Bhramarambika (Parvati as Shakti Peetha - 'goddess of bees')
Nandi (large pillared-hall idol facing the sanctum)
Five lingas said to have been installed by the Pandavas

history.dynasty: Satavahana origins; Chalukya, Kakatiya and Vijayanagara patronage; Chhatrapati Shivaji funded the northern gopuram (1667)
history.period: 1st century AD inscriptional reference (Satavahana king Vasisthiputra Pulumavi, Nasik inscription); present structure mainly 7th-18th century
history.summary: Srisailam Mallikarjuna Temple is one of the 12 Jyotirlingas of Shiva and also one of the 18 Shakti Peethas (Goddess Bhramaramba) - the only site holding both, per exploreoffbeat. Perched in the Nallamala Hills on the Krishna riverbank, its earliest inscriptional trace is the 1st-century AD Nasik inscription of Satavahana king Vasisthiputra Pulumavi; one account credits queen Trailokyamahadevi, wife of Chalukya king Vikramaditya II, with the 7th-century temple, and later Chalukyas, Kakatiyas and Vijayanagara rulers added mandapas and gopurams in Dravidian-Vijayanagara style. Legend says Parashurama installed the lingam, and that Shiva and Parvati settled here after consoling their son Karthikeya. CSV corrections: CSV town 'Kurnool' is WRONG - the temple town is Srisailam itself, ~200 km from Kurnool city; CSV's district was Kurnool, but since the 2022 AP district reorganization Srisailam falls in Nandyal district (geocoder confirms Nandyal).

name: Srisailam Mallikarjuna Temple
town_description: Srisailam is a temple town deep in the Nallamala forest of the Eastern Ghats, on the banks of the Krishna River. It is one of India's great Shaivite pilgrimage centres, built entirely around the Mallikarjuna Jyotirlinga and the Bhramaramba Shakti Peetha. The town lies inside a tiger-reserve forest, so vehicular entry is restricted to 6 AM-6 PM; besides the temple, it draws visitors to Pathalaganga (the river ghats at the hill base) and the Srisailam Dam.

travel.airport: Hyderabad (Rajiv Gandhi International, approx. 220 km) is the best-connected airport; Kurnool Airport is closer (approx. 190 km) but has limited flights (verify).
travel.railway: Markapur Road (approx. 80 km) is the nearest railway station, per onedaytravel; Kurnool (~180 km) for more trains.
travel.road: Srisailam is about 220 km by road from Hyderabad and ~180-200 km from Kurnool; APSRTC buses run from Hyderabad, Vijayawada, Kurnool and Nandyal. Entry into Srisailam is allowed only 6 AM-6 PM as it lies in a forest reserve (thetemples.in).

visitor_information.best_time: October to February for the pleasantest weather (sanatandharmaa); Maha Shivaratri and Navaratri are the grandest festivals but extremely crowded; avoid peak summer heat.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning 6:00 AM to 3:30 PM and evening 6:00 PM to 10:00 PM per xploringdestinations and thetemples.in (one source, sanatandharmaa, says 4:30 AM to 10:00 PM with an afternoon break - verify locally). Free general darshan; paid sevas (Suprabhata, Abhishekam, Rudrabhishekam, Sheeghra darshan) available; traditional dress code; photography not allowed inside.
